title: Teaching the practised thief
literal_meaning: Teaching an old hand at theft how to steal!
explanation: The dictionary places this exclamation under a thief practised in the activity, separately from an elderly thief. Its joke makes the lesson unnecessary because the learner already knows the craft. Our everyday application questions instruction offered without first finding out what someone knows; it neither praises theft nor says experienced people cannot learn.
meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନର ଏହି ଅର୍ଥରେ ଚୋରଟି ଚୋରିରେ ପାରଙ୍ଗମ; କେବଳ ବୟସରେ ବୁଢ଼ା ନୁହେଁ। ଯିଏ କାମଟି ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣେ, ତାକୁ ସେହି କାମ ଶିଖାଇବାରେ କଥାର ମଜା। ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ଶିଖାଇବା ଆଗରୁ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ କେତେ ଜାଣନ୍ତି, ତାହା ବୁଝିବା ଦରକାର। ଏହା ଚୋରିର ପ୍ରଶଂସା ବା ଅଭିଜ୍ଞ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଆଉ ଶିଖିବାର ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ରାୟ ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: An unnecessary lesson becomes the joke; our application asks about prior experience.
odia_summary: ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣିଥିବା କାମ ଶିଖାଇବାକୁ ନେଇ ମଜା; ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ପୂର୍ବ ଅଭିଜ୍ଞତାକୁ ଜାଣିବା ଜରୁରୀ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ନୂଆ ସହକର୍ମୀ ଫାଇଲ ସଜାଇବା ଶିଖାଇବାକୁ ଯାଉଥିଲେ। ରୀତା କହିଲେ, “ଏହି ପଦ୍ଧତିଟା ମୁଁ ତିଆରି କରିଥିଲି; ତୁମ ପାଖରେ କିଛି ନୂଆ ଉପାୟ ଅଛି କି?” / A colleague begins explaining a filing method to its creator, who remains open to improvements. This scene is invented.
cultural_context: The saying accompanies sense1, proficiency through practice. Sense2 separately describes an elderly thief. Neither establishes a real offender or an age-group trait.
